name: Karate
energy: Kumite is mostly aerobic (about 78%) with 1.5 s explosive actions in a 1:1.5 effort to pause pattern; kata is 1.5-3 min of continuous controlled power.
summary: Karate is won with fast, light-load power: winners produce more power at 30% of max, not more max strength. The plan builds explosive single-leg and rotational power, kicking hip strength and repeat-effort fitness, with knee and ankle prevention.

evidence.claim: In official kumite, high-intensity actions last about 1.5 s, the effort to pause ratio is about 1:1.5, and blood lactate reaches about 11 mmol/L.
evidence.source: Chaabene et al. 2014, Asian Journal of Sports Medicine

evidence.claim: Winners of national-team kumite bouts produced about 23% more upper-limb and 11% more lower-limb power at 30% of one-rep max, with no difference in maximal strength or jump height.
evidence.source: Roschel et al. 2009, Journal of Sports Science and Medicine

evidence.claim: Kumite causes about 88 injuries per 1000 athlete-exposures, mostly minor head and neck contusions.
evidence.source: Lystad et al. 2020, British Journal of Sports Medicine

variants.name: Kumite (sparring)
variants.desc: Repeated 1.5 s explosive attacks, fast footwork and pivots, with head contact.
variants.note: Your plan adds split-stance jumps for explosive entries and short neck work, and pre-season has bout-length intervals.

add.note: Fast off the floor, fighting stance

variants.name: Kata (forms)
variants.desc: 1.5-3 min of controlled power from deep stances, with high hip range and sharp stops.
variants.note: Your plan adds isometric split squat holds at stance depth and loaded hip mobility, and drops bout intervals for kata-length efforts.

add.note: Hold your deepest stance, no knee pain

slots.note: Knee above hip, control the lowering
Inner and outer hip for kicking

pre.name: Speed-strength lower
pre.focus: Light, fast loads and reactive jumps

slots.note: Light load, about 30% of your max, move it as fast as you can

off.name: Aerobic base
off.why: Kumite is mostly aerobic; a big base speeds recovery between exchanges and bouts.

pre.name: Bout intervals
pre.work: 3-4 rounds of 2-3 min: 2 s all-out burst (pads, shadow or bike), then 3 s of light footwork
pre.why: Matches the 1:1.5 effort to pause pattern of a bout.

pre.name: Kata-length efforts
pre.work: 4-6 x your longest kata at full intensity
pre.why: Trains power that holds up for 1.5-3 min.

tests.name: Countermovement jump
tests.how: Hands on hips, jump app or mat, best of 3.
tests.note: Elite mixed men and women averaged about 37 cm. Women about 20% lower than men.

tests.name: 10 m sprint
tests.how: Start 0.5 m behind the line, phone slow-motion video, best of 3.
tests.note: Kumite athletes are faster over 10 m than kata athletes. Bands are a coaching guide.

tests.name: Yo-Yo intermittent recovery level 1
tests.how: 20 m shuttles to beeps with 10 s jog recovery, until you miss two beeps.

tests.name: Y-balance anterior reach
tests.how: Stand on one leg, reach forward with the other foot, best of 3 each side.
tests.note: A left-right gap over 4 cm is a flag.

tests.name: Side split
tests.how: Slide into a side split against a wall, measure floor to crotch.
tests.note: Kata athletes track hip range here. Compare with yourself.

week: Hard sparring is the hard day: never lift heavy legs the day before it.
Heavy lower 3-4 days before a tournament at the latest.
Upper and rotation can go 2 days out.
Day before competing: rest or a 15 min primer.
primer: 2 x 3 med ball punches per side
Short, sharp footwork and pad work

lines: Last heavy lower session 7 days out.
Cut gym sets by about half; keep loads heavy and fast.
Last hard sparring or bout intervals 4-5 days out.
Weight classes: make weight by diet, not dehydration.

rules: No heavy legs or high-volume jumps the day before hard sparring or competition.
Mouthguard and approved protection for all sparring.
No dehydration weight cuts for amateurs, and none at all for under-18s.
Kata: train deep stances only to a depth you can hold without knee pain.
